events.what: Boij, Dannetun and Lundqvist prove Fröberg's conjecture in the second non-trivial degree for generic forms of degree d>2, and up to degree 2d-1 for sufficiently many variables
Wang and Zhang prove Fröberg's conjecture for r general forms of degree 5 or 7 in four variables, for every r>=1
events.ai_basis: The main results of this paper were obtained through a generative-AI workflow ... for the formulation of mathematical ideas, generation of conjectures and proof strategies, derivation and checking of intermediate steps, construction of examples and exact certificates

judgement.doubts: Both events are cases (restricted degrees/variables), both unreviewed; VibeMathed's recomputation of the Macaulay-matrix endpoints is automated/third-party corroboration, not digestion, and it did not check the reduction. Same tier, neither supersedes the other, so per Step 4 the AI role is the stronger one (Wang–Zhang). 'Assisted' vs 'generated' is close: 'main results ... obtained through a generative-AI workflow' with AI producing proof strategies and certificates leans toward generated, but the quote does not say humans only checked; kept assisted.

corrections.why: F9: kept, with doubt. The Wang–Zhang disclosure says the 'main results ... were obtained through a generative-AI workflow' with AI generating proof strategies, intermediate derivations and exact certificates, which could support 'generated'; but it does not state that humans only verified, so 'assisted' is the code the quote supports without inference.
